# Buttons and Links

Every button belongs to a tier, and the tier sets how much it stands out. As a rule: the tier decides priority, color decides emphasis, and an icon adds clarity. Buttons start an action; links take the reader somewhere. The Button, TextLink and Hyperlink pages list every configuration with its name, tokens and use.

## Buttons

### Tiers

![Three tiers: Tier 1 primary, red filled Get a Demo and Download buttons; Tier 2 secondary, red and blue outlined Learn More and Join Waitlist; Tier 3 utility, blue text links Show All and Next.](data:image/webp;base64,)

Three tiers, from most to least important. Tier 1, primary, drives business outcomes: form fills, trials, demos and sign-ups. Tier 2, secondary, helps people explore, compare or keep learning. Tier 3, utility, covers navigation, small actions and states. A higher tier stands out more, so people take the important action first.

### Tier 1: primary (conversion)

Red filled: `primary`, or `primary-inverted` on dark and photo grounds. A darker red on hover, gray when disabled. Large or small, never next to another primary. An icon is optional and only for a universal action, such as Download or Book a Meeting.

| Label | Icon |
| --- | --- |
| Try Now | No |
| Register Now / Register | No |
| Book Now / Book a Meeting | Yes |
| Sign Up | No |
| Get a Demo / Schedule a Demo | Yes |
| Start Free Trial (in a hero too) | No |
| Speak to an Expert | Yes |
| Download | Yes |
| Join Us / Join the Event | No |
| Subscribe Now | Yes |
| Get Your Free Report | Yes |
| Read Whitepaper | Yes |
| Contact Us | Yes |
| Save | Yes |
| Request a Call / Email | Yes |

### Tier 2: secondary (supportive)

Outlined in red, blue or white, depending on the ground: `secondary`, `secondary-alt` and `secondary-inverted`. Filled on hover, gray when disabled. Usually small or large inside modules. An icon is recommended when it makes the action clearer.

| Label | Color | Icon |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Learn More | Blue | Yes |
| Discover More | Blue | Yes |
| View All Events | Blue | Yes |
| See All Solutions | Blue | Yes |
| View Case Study | Blue | Yes |
| Watch the Video | Blue | Yes |
| Start Learning Now / Start Learning | Blue | Yes |
| Start Exam | Blue | Yes |
| Self Paced | Blue | No |
| Instructor Led | Blue | No |
| Submit | Blue | No |
| Submit a Session | Blue | Yes |
| Add to Calendar | Blue | Yes |
| Read the Report | Blue | Yes |
| Get the Guide | Blue | Yes |
| Learn How | Blue | Yes |

### Tier 3: utility (navigation, information and status)

For navigation, small actions and states that matter less. Usually a blue text link; small or large. An icon is highly recommended: it makes the action instant to read. In Flex, a text action is a blue TextLink (or a Hyperlink inside a sentence). Flex has no gray or black outlined button, so an outlined utility action uses the small blue outline (`secondary-alt`, `sm`).

| Label | Color | Style | Hover | Icon |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Next | Gray or blue | Text, underlined | Darker underline | Yes |
| Previous | Gray or blue | Text, underlined | Darker underline | Yes |
| Show All | Blue | Gray outline, or text | Blue fill | No |
| FAQs / Frequently Asked Questions | Blue | Text, underlined | Blue fill | Yes |
| Sold Out | Blue | Gray fill, or disabled | Blue fill | Yes |
| Search | Blue | Text, underlined | Blue fill | Yes, by exception |
| Look for These Signs | Blue | Text, underlined | Blue fill | Yes |
| Join Waitlist | Blue | Gray outline | Blue fill | Yes, by exception |
| Login | Blue | Text, underlined | Blue fill | Yes |
| Logout | Blue | Text, underlined | Blue fill | Yes |
| Retry / Refresh | Blue | Gray outline | Blue fill | Yes |
| Apply | Gray or red | Outline | Blue fill | No, or optional |

## Do's and don'ts

### Title Case

![Do: Try Now and Speak to an Expert in Title Case. Do not: try now and speak to an expert in mixed cases.](data:image/webp;base64,)

Use Title Case for every button label; don't mix cases.

### Space between a pair

![Do: a button pair 8px apart. Do not: the same pair spread far apart.](data:image/webp;base64,)

8px (`spacing-3xs`) between two buttons side by side; don't spread them apart.

### Short labels

![Do: Sign Up for Access, under 20 characters. Do not: a long lowercase sentence as a label.](data:image/webp;base64,)

Keep a label under 20 characters; don't write a sentence when a few words will do.

### One primary

![Do: a primary button beside a secondary button. Do not: two primary buttons side by side.](data:image/webp;base64,)

Pair a primary with a secondary button or a text link, never with another primary.

### Two at most

![Do: two buttons in a row. Do not: three buttons, two of them primary.](data:image/webp;base64,)

No more than two buttons in one row.

### Verbs

![Do: View Data Sheet. Do not: Datasheet.](data:image/webp;base64,)

Start with a verb that says what happens ("View Data Sheet"); don't use a passive label or a noun ("Datasheet").

### Hierarchy on the page

![Two page wireframes: one primary button with outlined Read More buttons below, marked right; every button filled red, marked wrong.](data:image/webp;base64,)

Keep the primary for the main conversion; repeated actions, such as "Read More" on a row of cards, use the secondary button or a text link.

## Mobile sizing

### Tier 1 on mobile

![Two phones: a form with a full-width Sign Up button for tier 1, and cards with a content-width Load More button for tier 2.](data:image/webp;base64,)

Always full width: it spans its container, label centered.

### Tier 2 on mobile

As wide as its label, not stretched by default; centered or left-aligned, following the layout.

## Links

### Inline hyperlinks

Inline hyperlinks sit inside a sentence or paragraph. They take the reader to related reference material or another page without breaking the flow of reading. A hyperlink is blue (`hyperlink-default`), SemiBold (at least two weights heavier than the copy around it) and always underlined; it turns a darker blue on hover.

### Underline

![Do: a blue, SemiBold, underlined link in a paragraph. Do not: the same link in blue with no underline.](data:image/webp;base64,)

Don't rely on color alone; the underline tells the link apart from the copy, including for people with color blindness.

### Sources

![Do: a source URL in blue and underlined. Do not: the URL in bold black.](data:image/webp;base64,)

Source lines and URLs are blue and underlined, like any other link.

### Dark grounds

![On a blue ground. Do: a white underlined link. Do not: white bold text with no underline.](data:image/webp;base64,)

On a dark or blue ground use the inverted (white) hyperlink, still underlined.

### Clean URLs

![Do: a short, clean URL. Do not: a long URL with tracking strings.](data:image/webp;base64,)

When a URL is shown, keep it short; drop tracking strings and extra characters.

### Say where it goes

![Do: the link is on the words Hero Group. Do not: a link on the words click here.](data:image/webp;base64,)

Link the words that describe the destination, never "click here" or "read more"; keep arrows and icons out of a wrapping paragraph, where they upset the line height.

### Links as navigation

![Two lists of links used as navigation; the hovered link shows a blue arrow.](data:image/webp;base64,)

A list of links that works as navigation may show an arrow on hover.

### Text link buttons

A text link button (also called a ghost, naked or tertiary button) looks like a link but acts like a button. It stands on its own, outside a paragraph: at the foot of a card, under a section, or beside a primary button.

### Outside the paragraph

![Do: a card with a text link button at its foot. Do not: a text link button with its arrow inside a sentence.](data:image/webp;base64,)

Don't put a text link button, with its arrow, inside running copy; place it at the end of the block.
